stem: Determine between which two consecutive integers the following irrational number lies, without using a calculator. Give the smaller integer first. $\sqrt{{=N}}$
solution: Find the perfect squares on either side of ${=N}$: ${=n}^{2} = {=n ** 2}$ and ${=n + 1}^{2} = {=(n + 1) ** 2}$.
notes: Same skeleton as the book's ex1-11-20a to d (find the two perfect squares that sandwich the radicand), with larger radicands than the book prints (the book stops at root 30; here the lower integer n runs 6 to 12, so the radicand runs 37 to 168 and the squares needed are 36 up to 169). The radicand is n^2 + r with 1 <= r <= 2n, so it is strictly between consecutive squares, is never a perfect square, and the answer is always n and n + 1. The stem adds 'Give the smaller integer first' only to make the two-value answer unambiguous. Basic tier (book) already covers the small radicands, so this tier is the same method at the size of numbers a Grade 10 learner is expected to recall (squares to 13^2).
